slide.text: Lagos faces a scale and coordination challenge
For Lagos State, land administration is not a back-office issue. It shapes housing delivery, builder confidence, corridor management, service trust, and the visibility of land-linked public value.

text.p: Lagos carries intense development pressure across housing estates, mixed-use sites, transport corridors, and fast-growing peri-urban districts. When parcel records, Certificate of Occupancy workflows, approvals, and field evidence remain fragmented, the state loses speed, visibility, and defensibility.

The real institutional cost is broader than delay. It includes slower project conversion, lower applicant confidence, higher coordination burden between desks, and weaker visibility into the land-linked value that should be traceable through state workflows.

p.strong: This is why Lagos should procure workflow infrastructure that connects parcel context, legal progression, field verification, and revenue assurance in one operating environment.

tr.td: Why it matters in Lagos procurement terms
Backlogs or opaque progression weaken service confidence and make it harder for leadership to understand where intervention is needed.
Housing, transport, right-of-way, and utility projects require parcel-aware review rather than disconnected file-by-file decisions.
Slow or unclear approval chains increase idle capital, delay delivery, and raise the final cost of formal projects.
The state needs a clearer line of sight from application activity to formalisation, obligations, and auditable public value capture.

slide.text: For Lagos, the procurement case is simple: improve service speed, title continuity, project predictability, and state revenue assurance from the same platform backbone.
